W5 (contrarian), after E028. All forecasts start from the E027 tip: 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0–2, but only 0.7526 on held-out seeds 3–12. The true mean is below the bar, so a booster is needed before any further cut. A 3-seed draw has an SD of about 0.25 pp, and a schedule change that leaves RNG use alone still lets the trajectories diverge, so single runs cannot separate effects under about 0.3 pp.

Mechanism the others have missed: two step-count windows are coupled to the resolution phases.
- The whitening bias trains for a fixed 75 steps (3 epochs × 25). At 219 total steps that covers all of the 20 px phase and nearly all of the 24 px phase, and it ends before 28 px starts (step 88).
- The LR peak comes at step 50, inside the 24 px phase.
So the stem bias is fitted only on low-resolution statistics and then frozen. Tail resolutions have to re-adapt through BN and group 1. This also explains why E028 (cutting group-1 backprop in the tail) hurt, and why late low-res or big jumps (E011, E018, E024) hurt while early low-res (E026) was nearly free.

Implications:
- Taking more early steps at low res (I050) leaves the stem even more biased toward low-res statistics, so it costs more than E026's free lunch suggests.
- Per-resolution whitening (I051) or a whitening bias that trains again in the tail are the only boosters with a mechanism behind them.
- Hyperparameter knobs (wd, LS, Muon lr, averaging) sit on a plateau of ±0.2 pp. I expect I047–I049 to read as noise.

Time model: roughly 25 ms per 32 px step plus about 0.4 s fixed. Moving 15% of steps from 24 px to 20 px saves about 0.17 s (E026). Lookahead, LS and LR changes are time-neutral to within 0.03 s.

forecasts.reason: With the warm-up halved, the peak moves to about step 25, inside the 20 px phase while the whitening bias is still training. Muon renormalizes the filters, so the LR shape matters less. The expected effect is near zero and well inside the noise.

Averaging knobs are on a plateau, and E025 showed that changing the averaging dynamics hurts more often than it helps. Halving the number of updates saves about 0.02 s. A gain of 0.15 pp or more is unlikely.

CIFAR-100 short runs are under-fitting, and LS 0.3 with a 1/9 logit scale is tuned as a pair. Dropping LS late shifts the logit scale just while the average is forming, which is a mild negative to neutral.

The time saving roughly matches E026's (about −0.17 s, close to the 2.5% threshold). Under my mechanism, though, the whitening bias and the LR peak would both sit mostly at 20 px, so I expect a held-out loss of about 0.2–0.3 pp, which breaks the 0.15 pp limit.
This is the only idea that targets the stem-statistics mismatch. Expect +0.1 to +0.3 pp. The cost is three extra eigh decompositions plus 5k-image resizes in timed prepare, about +0.04 s.

cruxes: Is the low-resolution cost a stem-statistics mismatch? Two cheap tests would settle it: per-resolution whitening (I051), or letting the whitening bias train again during the 32 px tail. Either one recovering 0.2 pp or more held-out would reopen the low-res time lever.

Does the fixed 75-step whitening-bias window interact with the resolution phases and the step count? It ends before 28 px starts, and every epoch trim pushes it further into the run. An ablation that expresses it as a fraction of steps would show whether part of the epoch-dial loss is really stem freezing.

With the E027 held-out mean at 0.7526, the tip's true mean is below the bar. Can any time-neutral booster deliver 0.2 pp or more held-out? If none can, the best path is to buy back about 0.25 epoch, not to cut further.
